BAS2-01.note: Fronting 'for the summer program' is marginal at best.

BAS2-03.note: 'His old phone nobody could convince my grandfather to replace' is a marginal topicalization.

BAS2-04.note: 'By a professional we had the old piano tuned' is marginal or archaic.

BAS2-05.note: 'With the move she got her brother to help' (topic fronting) is marginal and normally wants a comma.

BAS2-06.note: The correlative chips lock the order.

alternatives: so long | was | the lecture | that | several students | fell asleep
BAS2-09.note: Inversion after a fronted 'so + adjective' ('So long was the lecture that...') is standard, if literary, English and uses exactly the same chips.

BAS2-10.note: 'Whether the store is still open I wonder' is marginal.

alternatives: why | the meeting | was cancelled | nobody | knows
BAS2-11.note: Topicalizing the wh-clause ('Why the meeting was cancelled, nobody knows') is idiomatic. It usually takes a comma, but it reads fine without one. Also marginal: 'the meeting was cancelled nobody knows why', which is a run-on without punctuation.

BAS2-12.note: 'How the ancient bridge was built the guide explained' is marginal.

BAS2-13.note: 'Who found the lost keys? It was my neighbor' needs added punctuation, so it is excluded.

BAS2-14.note: 'In this room it was that the treaty was signed' is archaic or marginal.

BAS2-17.note: Marginal: 'My parents grew up where the village has no hospital' is grammatical, but the definite 'the village' and the past/present tense mix make it odd. Worth a second look.

BAS2-19.note: Swapping the noun phrases gives nonsense.

BAS2-20.note: 'to show to the guard their tickets' is a heavy-NP shift with an NP that is too light, so it is unnatural.

alternatives: researchers | discovered | that | without oxygen | the bacteria | could survive
BAS2-22.note: Fronting the PP inside the that-clause is grammatical and natural. Marginal: 'that the bacteria without oxygen could survive'.

alternatives: the speed | of the recovery | was | what | surprised | everyone

BAS2-24.note: 'The weather depends on whether the plan will work' is grammatical, but the meaning is absurd.

BAS2-29.note: 'Her design the judges considered the most original' is a marginal topicalization.

BAS2-31.note: 'To repair the bridge it took the workers three months' is marginal and needs a comma.

BAS2-32.note: 'If I had a library card the librarian asked' reads as a conditional with an incomplete meaning, so it is marginal.

BAS2-33.note: 'Why the project failed there are several reasons' is marginal.

BAS2-35.note: 'The mail carrier kept barking at the neighbors' dog' is grammatical, but semantically odd unless 'barking' is read as shouting.

alternatives: my first summer job | always reminds | me | of | that song
BAS2-38.note: Swapping the noun phrases gives a fully grammatical, natural sentence with a different meaning.

BAS2-44.note: 'For the whole family my grandmother used to sew dresses' is marginal.

BAS2-45.note: The 'I seen' chip forces inversion after 'have'. None found.
